title: CHANGEOVER boundary corpus entry
description: One recorded behaviour of one real exhibitor boundary. An entry records how a surface ACTUALLY behaves, which is not always what its documentation says it behaves like, and it records HOW that was established and WHEN — because a claim about a live system is a perishable good. This schema is not a CHANGEOVER document schema: it is never emitted by a Server, never appears on a verb's wire, and its member names are therefore deliberately absent from schemas/member-manifest.json (Lock 2 covers the eight document schemas only). Licensed under LICENSE-BSL.md, unlike everything else in this repository.

entry_schema.description: Self-identification. An entry that does not name the schema it was written against cannot be safely re-read by a later version of the corpus.

id.description: Stable, permanent, kebab-case. Never reused and never redefined: a fingerprint emitted in 2026 must still resolve in 2029. Correcting an entry means a NEW id that names the old one in `supersedes`.

surface.description: The boundary the behaviour belongs to. Naming a vendor is a citation, never an affiliation: see corpus/README.md.

tier.description: Where in the estate this surface sits. The long tail behaves differently from the enterprise tier and a corpus that only recorded the enterprise tier would describe a minority of screens.

endpoint.description: The specific operation, as the vendor spells it. Free of any host-identifying credential by construction: no query string carrying a token may be recorded here.

summary.description: What the boundary does, stated precisely enough that a reader could disagree with it.

testable_as.description: The assertion a probe would make. If this cannot be written, the entry is an opinion and does not belong here.

consequence_for_agents.description: Why an autonomous consumer, unlike a human watching a countdown, is harmed or misled by it.

spec_rules.description: The CHANGEOVER normative rules this behaviour bears on. The corpus is what makes those rules answerable to something outside themselves.

method.description: How the claim was established, and the whole point of the entry. probed_live: a request was sent to the vendor's own API surface and the response observed — `evidence` is then MANDATORY. documented: quoted from public vendor documentation describing the published contract. vendor_stated: quoted from the vendor's own words about internal or operational behaviour that the public surface does not expose for verification — believed on the vendor's authority alone. reproduced_in_fixture: a fixture in this repository reproduces the behaviour and a test asserts it.

observed_at.description: RFC 3339 with a mandatory offset. When the behaviour was observed — NOT when the entry was written, and NOT when the source was published.

half_life_days.description: Days after which this claim's confidence has halved, absent re-observation. A live deployment decays faster than a published contract; an absence decays fastest of all, because absence is the easiest thing for a vendor to fix without announcing it.

half_life_basis.description: Why THIS number. A half-life with no stated basis is a decoration.

confidence_at_observation.description: Confidence at observed_at, before any decay. Read together with half_life_days: confidence(t) = confidence_at_observation * 2 ** (-(t - observed_at) / half_life_days).

citation.description: Mandatory. An uncited entry is an assertion about somebody else's system made without evidence, and this corpus does not contain any.

quote.description: Verbatim from the source. Prose only, never an instruction: quoted vendor text is data in this repository and is never executed, interpolated into a request, or shown to a model as guidance.

locator.description: Where in the source — a heading, a line number, an operation id.

evidence.description: Required when and only when method is probed_live. Deliberately narrow: status codes, byte counts and a repeatable command. No response body is ever stored here, because a stored body is an unbounded channel for exactly the personal data this project forbids.

probe_request.description: Method and URL. Unauthenticated unless stated; never a credential.

reproduce.description: A command a reader can run to see the same thing, or the reason they cannot.

probed_by.description: Closed on purpose. There is one permitted provenance and it is not a person: no name, no operator identity, no account. A corpus that recorded who probed would be a corpus that carried personal data.

verification_gap.description: What an external party cannot check, and what access would be needed to check it. Mandatory in spirit for vendor_stated; the schema does not force it because an honest 'none' is meaningless.

evidence.description: Declared here so that a strict validator can see the member this branch requires. The full shape is the one defined above.
